kn: ತಂ ತಥಾ ಕೃಪಯಾವಿಷ್ಟಮಶ್ರುಪೂರ್ಣಾಕುಲೇಕ್ಷಣಮ್ ವಿಷೀದನ್ತಮಿದಂ ವಾಕ್ಯಮುವಾಚ ಮಧುಸೂದನಃ
roman: taṃ tathā kṛpayāviṣṭamaśrupūrṇākulekṣaṇam viṣīdantamidaṃ vākyamuvāca madhusūdanaḥ
trans: Sanjay said: Seeing Arjun overwhelmed with pity, his mind grief-stricken, and his eyes full of tears, Shree Krishna spoke the following words.

kn: ಕುತಸ್ತ್ವಾ ಕಶ್ಮಲಮಿದಂ ವಿಷಮೇ ಸಮುಪಸ್ಥಿತಮ್ ಅನಾರ್ಯಜುಷ್ಟಮಸ್ವರ್ಗ್ಯಮಕೀರ್ತಿಕರಮರ್ಜುನ
roman: kutastvā kaśmalamidaṃ viṣame samupasthitam anāryajuṣṭamasvargyamakīrtikaramarjuna
trans: The Supreme Lord said: My dear Arjun, how has this delusion overcome you in this hour of peril? It is not befitting an honorable person. It leads not to the higher abodes, but to disgrace.

kn: ಕ್ಲೈಬ್ಯಂ ಮಾ ಸ್ಮ ಗಮಃ ಪಾರ್ಥ ನೈತತ್ತ್ವಯ್ಯುಪಪದ್ಯತೇ ಕ್ಷುದ್ರಂ ಹೃದಯದೌರ್ಬಲ್ಯಂ ತ್ಯಕ್ತ್ವೋತ್ತಿಷ್ಠ ಪರನ್ತಪ
roman: klaibyaṃ mā sma gamaḥ pārtha naitattvayyupapadyate kṣudraṃ hṛdayadaurbalyaṃ tyaktvottiṣṭha parantapa
trans: O Parth, it does not befit you to yield to this unmanliness. Give up such petty weakness of heart and arise, O vanquisher of enemies.

kn: ಕಥಂ ಭೀಷ್ಮಮಹಂ ಸಙ್ಖ್ಯೇ ದ್ರೋಣಂ ಚ ಮಧುಸೂದನ ಇಷುಭಿಃ ಪ್ರತಿಯೋತ್ಸ್ಯಾಮಿ ಪೂಜಾರ್ಹಾವರಿಸೂದನ
roman: kathaṃ bhīṣmamahaṃ saṅkhye droṇaṃ ca madhusūdana iṣubhiḥ pratiyotsyāmi pūjārhāvarisūdana
trans: Arjun said: O Madhusudan, how can I shoot arrows in battle on men like Bheeshma and Dronacharya, who are worthy of my worship, O destroyer of enemies?

kn: ಗುರೂನಹತ್ವಾ ಹಿ ಮಹಾನುಭಾವಾನ್ ಶ್ರೇಯೋ ಭೋಕ್ತುಂ ಭೈಕ್ಷ್ಯಮಪೀಹ ಲೋಕೇ ಹತ್ವಾರ್ಥಕಾಮಾಂಸ್ತು ಗುರೂನಿಹೈವ ಭುಞ್ಜೀಯ ಭೋಗಾನ್ ರುಧಿರಪ್ರದಿಗ್ಧಾನ್
roman: gurūnahatvā hi mahānubhāvān śreyo bhoktuṃ bhaikṣyamapīha loke hatvārthakāmāṃstu gurūnihaiva bhuñjīya bhogān rudhirapradigdhān
trans: It would be better to live in this world by begging, than to enjoy life by killing these noble elders, who are my teachers. If we kill them, the wealth and pleasures we enjoy will be tainted with blood.

kn: ನ ಚೈತದ್ವಿದ್ಮಃ ಕತರನ್ನೋ ಗರೀಯೋ ಯದ್ವಾ ಜಯೇಮ ಯದಿ ವಾ ನೋ ಜಯೇಯುಃ ಯಾನೇವ ಹತ್ವಾ ನ ಜಿಜೀವಿಷಾಮಸ್ತೇಽವಸ್ಥಿತಾಃ ಪ್ರಮುಖೇ ಧಾರ್ತರಾಷ್ಟ್ರಾಃ
roman: na caitadvidmaḥ kataranno garīyo yadvā jayema yadi vā no jayeyuḥ yāneva hatvā na jijīviṣāmaste'vasthitāḥ pramukhe dhārtarāṣṭrāḥ
trans: We do not even know which result of this war is preferable for us—conquering them or being conquered by them. Even after killing them we will not desire to live. Yet they have taken the side of the sons of Dhritarasthra, and now stand before us on the battlefield.

kn: ಕಾರ್ಪಣ್ಯದೋಷೋಪಹತಸ್ವಭಾವಃ ಪೃಚ್ಛಾಮಿ ತ್ವಾಂ ಧರ್ಮಸಮ್ಮೂಢಚೇತಾಃ ಯಚ್ಛ್ರೇಯಃ ಸ್ಯಾನ್ನಿಶ್ಚಿತಂ ಬ್ರೂಹಿ ತನ್ಮೇ ಶಿಷ್ಯಸ್ತೇಽಹಂ ಶಾಧಿ ಮಾಂ ತ್ವಾಂ ಪ್ರಪನ್ನಮ್
roman: kārpaṇyadoṣopahatasvabhāvaḥ pṛcchāmi tvāṃ dharmasammūḍhacetāḥ yacchreyaḥ syānniścitaṃ brūhi tanme śiṣyaste'haṃ śādhi māṃ tvāṃ prapannam
trans: I am confused about my duty, and am besieged with anxiety and faintheartedness. I am Your disciple, and am surrendered to You. Please instruct me for certain what is best for me.

kn: ನ ಹಿ ಪ್ರಪಶ್ಯಾಮಿ ಮಮಾಪನುದ್ಯಾದ್ಯಚ್ಛೋಕಮುಚ್ಛೋಷಣಮಿನ್ದ್ರಿಯಾಣಾಮ್ ಅವಾಪ್ಯ ಭೂಮಾವಸಪತ್ನಮೃದ್ಧಂ ರಾಜ್ಯಂ ಸುರಾಣಾಮಪಿ ಚಾಧಿಪತ್ಯಮ್
roman: na hi prapaśyāmi mamāpanudyādyacchokamucchoṣaṇamindriyāṇām avāpya bhūmāvasapatnamṛddhaṃ rājyaṃ surāṇāmapi cādhipatyam
trans: I can find no means of driving away this anguish that is drying up my senses. Even if I win a prosperous and unrivalled kingdom on the earth, or gain sovereignty like the celestial gods, I will be unable to dispel this grief.

kn: ಏವಮುಕ್ತ್ವಾ ಹೃಷೀಕೇಶಂ ಗುಡಾಕೇಶಃ ಪರನ್ತಪ ನ ಯೋತ್ಸ್ಯ ಇತಿ ಗೋವಿನ್ದಮುಕ್ತ್ವಾ ತೂಷ್ಣೀಂ ಬಭೂವ ಹ
roman: evamuktvā hṛṣīkeśaṃ guḍākeśaḥ parantapa na yotsya iti govindamuktvā tūṣṇīṃ babhūva ha
trans: Sanjay said: Having thus spoken, Gudakesh, that chastiser of enemies, addressed Hrishikesh: Govind, I shall not fight, and became silent.

kn: ತಮುವಾಚ ಹೃಷೀಕೇಶಃ ಪ್ರಹಸನ್ನಿವ ಭಾರತ ಸೇನಯೋರುಭಯೋರ್ಮಧ್ಯೇ ವಿಷೀದನ್ತಮಿದಂ ವಚಃ
roman: tamuvāca hṛṣīkeśaḥ prahasanniva bhārata senayorubhayormadhye viṣīdantamidaṃ vacaḥ
trans: O Dhritarashtra, thereafter, in the midst of both the armies, Shree Krishna smilingly spoke the following words to the grief-stricken Arjun.

kn: ಅಶೋಚ್ಯಾನನ್ವಶೋಚಸ್ತ್ವಂ ಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾವಾದಾಂಶ್ಚ ಭಾಷಸೇ ಗತಾಸೂನಗತಾಸೂಂಶ್ಚ ನಾನುಶೋಚನ್ತಿ ಪಣ್ಡಿತಾಃ
roman: aśocyānanvaśocastvaṃ prajñāvādāṃśca bhāṣase gatāsūnagatāsūṃśca nānuśocanti paṇḍitāḥ
trans: The Supreme Lord said: While you speak words of wisdom, you are mourning for that which is not worthy of grief. The wise lament neither for the living nor for the dead.

kn: ನ ತ್ವೇವಾಹಂ ಜಾತು ನಾಸಂ ನ ತ್ವಂ ನೇಮೇ ಜನಾಧಿಪಾಃ ನ ಚೈವ ನ ಭವಿಷ್ಯಾಮಃ ಸರ್ವೇ ವಯಮತಃ ಪರಮ್
roman: na tvevāhaṃ jātu nāsaṃ na tvaṃ neme janādhipāḥ na caiva na bhaviṣyāmaḥ sarve vayamataḥ param
trans: Never was there a time when I did not exist, nor you, nor all these kings; nor in the future shall any of us cease to be.

kn: ದೇಹಿನೋಽಸ್ಮಿನ್ಯಥಾ ದೇಹೇ ಕೌಮಾರಂ ಯೌವನಂ ಜರಾ ತಥಾ ದೇಹಾನ್ತರಪ್ರಾಪ್ತಿರ್ಧೀರಸ್ತತ್ರ ನ ಮುಹ್ಯತಿ
roman: dehino'sminyathā dehe kaumāraṃ yauvanaṃ jarā tathā dehāntaraprāptirdhīrastatra na muhyati
trans: Just as the embodied soul continuously passes from childhood to youth to old age, similarly, at the time of death, the soul passes into another body. The wise are not deluded by this.

kn: ಮಾತ್ರಾಸ್ಪರ್ಶಾಸ್ತು ಕೌನ್ತೇಯ ಶೀತೋಷ್ಣಸುಖದುಃಖದಾಃ ಆಗಮಾಪಾಯಿನೋಽನಿತ್ಯಾಸ್ತಾಂಸ್ತಿತಿಕ್ಷಸ್ವ ಭಾರತ
roman: mātrāsparśāstu kaunteya śītoṣṇasukhaduḥkhadāḥ āgamāpāyino'nityāstāṃstitikṣasva bhārata
trans: O son of Kunti, the contact between the senses and the sense objects gives rise to fleeting perceptions of happiness and distress. These are non-permanent, and come and go like the winter and summer seasons. O descendent of Bharat, one must learn to tolerate them without being disturbed.

kn: ಯಂ ಹಿ ನ ವ್ಯಥಯನ್ತ್ಯೇತೇ ಪುರುಷಂ ಪುರುಷರ್ಷಭ ಸಮದುಃಖಸುಖಂ ಧೀರಂ ಸೋಽಮೃತತ್ವಾಯ ಕಲ್ಪತೇ
roman: yaṃ hi na vyathayantyete puruṣaṃ puruṣarṣabha samaduḥkhasukhaṃ dhīraṃ so'mṛtatvāya kalpate
trans: O Arjun, noblest amongst men, that person who is not affected by happiness and distress, and remains steady in both, becomes eligible for liberation.

kn: ನಾಸತೋ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ ಭಾವೋ ನಾಭಾವೋ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ ಸತಃ ಉಭಯೋರಪಿ ದೃಷ್ಟೋಽನ್ತಸ್ತ್ವನಯೋಸ್ತತ್ತ್ವದರ್ಶಿಭಿಃ
roman: nāsato vidyate bhāvo nābhāvo vidyate sataḥ ubhayorapi dṛṣṭo'ntastvanayostattvadarśibhiḥ
trans: Of the transient there is no endurance, and of the eternal there is no cessation. This has verily been observed and concluded by the seers of the Truth, after studying the nature of both.

kn: ಅವಿನಾಶಿ ತು ತದ್ವಿದ್ಧಿ ಯೇನ ಸರ್ವಮಿದಂ ತತಮ್ ವಿನಾಶಮವ್ಯಯಸ್ಯಾಸ್ಯ ನ ಕಶ್ಚಿತ್ಕರ್ತುಮರ್ಹತಿ
roman: avināśi tu tadviddhi yena sarvamidaṃ tatam vināśamavyayasyāsya na kaścitkartumarhati
trans: That which pervades the entire body, know it to be indestructible. No one can cause the destruction of the imperishable soul.

kn: ಅನ್ತವನ್ತ ಇಮೇ ದೇಹಾ ನಿತ್ಯಸ್ಯೋಕ್ತಾಃ ಶರೀರಿಣಃ ಅನಾಶಿನೋಽಪ್ರಮೇಯಸ್ಯ ತಸ್ಮಾದ್ಯುಧ್ಯಸ್ವ ಭಾರತ
roman: antavanta ime dehā nityasyoktāḥ śarīriṇaḥ anāśino'prameyasya tasmādyudhyasva bhārata
trans: Only the material body is perishable; the embodied soul within is indestructible, immeasurable, and eternal. Therefore, fight, O descendent of Bharat.

kn: ಯ ಏನಂ ವೇತ್ತಿ ಹನ್ತಾರಂ ಯಶ್ಚೈನಂ ಮನ್ಯತೇ ಹತಮ್ ಉಭೌ ತೌ ನ ವಿಜಾನೀತೋ ನಾಯಂ ಹನ್ತಿ ನ ಹನ್ಯತೇ
roman: ya enaṃ vetti hantāraṃ yaścainaṃ manyate hatam ubhau tau na vijānīto nāyaṃ hanti na hanyate
trans: Neither of them is in knowledge—the one who thinks the soul can slay and the one who thinks the soul can be slain. For truly, the soul neither kills nor can it be killed.

kn: ನ ಜಾಯತೇ ಮ್ರಿಯತೇ ವಾ ಕದಾಚಿನ್ನಾಯಂ ಭೂತ್ವಾ ಭವಿತಾ ವಾ ನ ಭೂಯಃ ಅಜೋ ನಿತ್ಯಃ ಶಾಶ್ವತೋಽಯಂ ಪುರಾಣೋ ನ ಹನ್ಯತೇ ಹನ್ಯಮಾನೇ ಶರೀರೇ
roman: na jāyate mriyate vā kadācinnāyaṃ bhūtvā bhavitā vā na bhūyaḥ ajo nityaḥ śāśvato'yaṃ purāṇo na hanyate hanyamāne śarīre
trans: The soul is neither born, nor does it ever die; nor having once existed, does it ever cease to be. The soul is without birth, eternal, immortal, and ageless. It is not destroyed when the body is destroyed.

kn: ವೇದಾವಿನಾಶಿನಂ ನಿತ್ಯಂ ಯ ಏನಮಜಮವ್ಯಯಮ್ ಕಥಂ ಸ ಪುರುಷಃ ಪಾರ್ಥ ಕಂ ಘಾತಯತಿ ಹನ್ತಿ ಕಮ್
roman: vedāvināśinaṃ nityaṃ ya enamajamavyayam kathaṃ sa puruṣaḥ pārtha kaṃ ghātayati hanti kam
trans: O Parth, how can one who knows the soul to be imperishable, eternal, unborn, and immutable kill anyone or cause anyone to kill?

kn: ವಾಸಾಂಸಿ ಜೀರ್ಣಾನಿ ಯಥಾ ವಿಹಾಯ ನವಾನಿ ಗೃಹ್ಣಾತಿ ನರೋಽಪರಾಣಿ ತಥಾ ಶರೀರಾಣಿ ವಿಹಾಯ ಜೀರ್ಣಾನ್ಯನ್ಯಾನಿ ಸಂಯಾತಿ ನವಾನಿ ದೇಹೀ
roman: vāsāṃsi jīrṇāni yathā vihāya navāni gṛhṇāti naro'parāṇi tathā śarīrāṇi vihāya jīrṇānyanyāni saṃyāti navāni dehī
trans: As a person sheds worn-out garments and wears new ones, likewise, at the time of death, the soul casts off its worn-out body and enters a new one.

kn: ನೈನಂ ಛಿನ್ದನ್ತಿ ಶಸ್ತ್ರಾಣಿ ನೈನಂ ದಹತಿ ಪಾವಕಃ ನ ಚೈನಂ ಕ್ಲೇದಯನ್ತ್ಯಾಪೋ ನ ಶೋಷಯತಿ ಮಾರುತಃ
roman: nainaṃ chindanti śastrāṇi nainaṃ dahati pāvakaḥ na cainaṃ kledayantyāpo na śoṣayati mārutaḥ
trans: Weapons cannot shred the soul, nor can fire burn it. Water cannot wet it, nor can the wind dry it.

kn: ಅಚ್ಛೇದ್ಯೋಽಯಮದಾಹ್ಯೋಽಯಮಕ್ಲೇದ್ಯೋಽಶೋಷ್ಯ ಏವ ಚ ನಿತ್ಯಃ ಸರ್ವಗತಃ ಸ್ಥಾಣುರಚಲೋಽಯಂ ಸನಾತನಃ
roman: acchedyo'yamadāhyo'yamakledyo'śoṣya eva ca nityaḥ sarvagataḥ sthāṇuracalo'yaṃ sanātanaḥ
trans: The soul is unbreakable and incombustible; it can neither be dampened nor dried. It is everlasting, in all places, unalterable, immutable, and primordial.

kn: ಅವ್ಯಕ್ತೋಽಯಮಚಿನ್ತ್ಯೋಽಯಮವಿಕಾರ್ಯೋಽಯಮುಚ್ಯತೇ ತಸ್ಮಾದೇವಂ ವಿದಿತ್ವೈನಂ ನಾನುಶೋಚಿತುಮರ್ಹಸಿ
roman: avyakto'yamacintyo'yamavikāryo'yamucyate tasmādevaṃ viditvainaṃ nānuśocitumarhasi
trans: The soul is spoken of as invisible, inconceivable, and unchangeable. Knowing this, you should not grieve for the body.

kn: ಅಥ ಚೈನಂ ನಿತ್ಯಜಾತಂ ನಿತ್ಯಂ ವಾ ಮನ್ಯಸೇ ಮೃತಮ್ ತಥಾಪಿ ತ್ವಂ ಮಹಾಬಾಹೋ ನೈವಂ ಶೋಚಿತುಮರ್ಹಸಿ
roman: atha cainaṃ nityajātaṃ nityaṃ vā manyase mṛtam tathāpi tvaṃ mahābāho naivaṃ śocitumarhasi
trans: If, however, you think that the self is subject to constant birth and death, O mighty-armed Arjun, even then you should not grieve like this.

kn: ಜಾತಸ್ಯ ಹಿ ಧ್ರುವೋ ಮೃತ್ಯುರ್ಧ್ರುವಂ ಜನ್ಮ ಮೃತಸ್ಯ ಚ ತಸ್ಮಾದಪರಿಹಾರ್ಯೇಽರ್ಥೇ ನ ತ್ವಂ ಶೋಚಿತುಮರ್ಹಸಿ
roman: jātasya hi dhruvo mṛtyurdhruvaṃ janma mṛtasya ca tasmādaparihārye'rthe na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi
trans: Death is certain for one who has been born, and rebirth is inevitable for one who has died. Therefore, you should not lament over the inevitable.

kn: ಅವ್ಯಕ್ತಾದೀನಿ ಭೂತಾನಿ ವ್ಯಕ್ತಮಧ್ಯಾನಿ ಭಾರತ ಅವ್ಯಕ್ತನಿಧನಾನ್ಯೇವ ತತ್ರ ಕಾ ಪರಿದೇವನಾ
roman: avyaktādīni bhūtāni vyaktamadhyāni bhārata avyaktanidhanānyeva tatra kā paridevanā
trans: O scion of Bharat, all created beings are unmanifest before birth, manifest in life, and again unmanifest on death. So why grieve?

kn: ಆಶ್ಚರ್ಯವತ್ಪಶ್ಯತಿ ಕಶ್ಚಿದೇನಮಾಶ್ಚರ್ಯವದ್ವದತಿ ತಥೈವ ಚಾನ್ಯಃ ಆಶ್ಚರ್ಯವಚ್ಚೈನಮನ್ಯಃ ಶೃಣೋತಿ ಶ್ರುತ್ವಾಪ್ಯೇನಂ ವೇದ ನ ಚೈವ ಕಶ್ಚಿತ್
roman: āścaryavatpaśyati kaścidenamāścaryavadvadati tathaiva cānyaḥ āścaryavaccainamanyaḥ śṛṇoti śrutvāpyenaṃ veda na caiva kaścit
trans: Some see the soul as amazing, some describe it as amazing, and some hear of the soul as amazing, while others, even on hearing, cannot understand it at all.

kn: ದೇಹೀ ನಿತ್ಯಮವಧ್ಯೋಽಯಂ ದೇಹೇ ಸರ್ವಸ್ಯ ಭಾರತ ತಸ್ಮಾತ್ಸರ್ವಾಣಿ ಭೂತಾನಿ ನ ತ್ವಂ ಶೋಚಿತುಮರ್ಹಸಿ
roman: dehī nityamavadhyo'yaṃ dehe sarvasya bhārata tasmātsarvāṇi bhūtāni na tvaṃ śocitumarhasi
trans: O Arjun, the soul that dwells within the body is immortal; therefore, you should not mourn for anyone.

kn: ಸ್ವಧರ್ಮಮಪಿ ಚಾವೇಕ್ಷ್ಯ ನ ವಿಕಮ್ಪಿತುಮರ್ಹಸಿ ಧರ್ಮ್ಯಾದ್ಧಿ ಯುದ್ಧಾಚ್ಛ್ರೇಯೋಽನ್ಯತ್ಕ್ಷತ್ರಿಯಸ್ಯ ನ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ
roman: svadharmamapi cāvekṣya na vikampitumarhasi dharmyāddhi yuddhācchreyo'nyatkṣatriyasya na vidyate
trans: Besides, considering your duty as a warrior, you should not waver. Indeed, for a warrior, there is no better engagement than fighting for upholding of righteousness.

kn: ಯದೃಚ್ಛಯಾ ಚೋಪಪನ್ನಂ ಸ್ವರ್ಗದ್ವಾರಮಪಾವೃತಮ್ ಸುಖಿನಃ ಕ್ಷತ್ರಿಯಾಃ ಪಾರ್ಥ ಲಭನ್ತೇ ಯುದ್ಧಮೀದೃಶಮ್
roman: yadṛcchayā copapannaṃ svargadvāramapāvṛtam sukhinaḥ kṣatriyāḥ pārtha labhante yuddhamīdṛśam
trans: O Parth, happy are the warriors to whom such opportunities to defend righteousness come unsought, opening for them the stairway to the celestial abodes.

kn: ಅಥ ಚೇತ್ತ್ವಮಿಮಂ ಧರ್ಮ್ಯಂ ಸಙ್ಗ್ರಾಮಂ ನ ಕರಿಷ್ಯಸಿ ತತಃ ಸ್ವಧರ್ಮಂ ಕೀರ್ತಿಂ ಚ ಹಿತ್ವಾ ಪಾಪಮವಾಪ್ಸ್ಯಸಿ
roman: atha cettvamimaṃ dharmyaṃ saṅgrāmaṃ na kariṣyasi tataḥ svadharmaṃ kīrtiṃ ca hitvā pāpamavāpsyasi
trans: If, however, you refuse to fight this righteous war, abandoning your social duty and reputation, you will certainly incur sin.

kn: ಅಕೀರ್ತಿಂ ಚಾಪಿ ಭೂತಾನಿ ಕಥಯಿಷ್ಯನ್ತಿ ತೇಽವ್ಯಯಾಮ್ ಸಮ್ಭಾವಿತಸ್ಯ ಚಾಕೀರ್ತಿರ್ಮರಣಾದತಿರಿಚ್ಯತೇ
roman: akīrtiṃ cāpi bhūtāni kathayiṣyanti te'vyayām sambhāvitasya cākīrtirmaraṇādatiricyate
trans: People will speak of you as a coward and a deserter. For a respectable person, infamy is worse than death.

kn: ಭಯಾದ್ರಣಾದುಪರತಂ ಮಂಸ್ಯನ್ತೇ ತ್ವಾಂ ಮಹಾರಥಾಃ ಯೇಷಾಂ ಚ ತ್ವಂ ಬಹುಮತೋ ಭೂತ್ವಾ ಯಾಸ್ಯಸಿ ಲಾಘವಮ್
roman: bhayādraṇāduparataṃ maṃsyante tvāṃ mahārathāḥ yeṣāṃ ca tvaṃ bahumato bhūtvā yāsyasi lāghavam
trans: The great generals who hold you in high esteem will think that you fled from the battlefield out of fear, and thus will lose their respect for you.

kn: ಅವಾಚ್ಯವಾದಾಂಶ್ಚ ಬಹೂನ್ವದಿಷ್ಯನ್ತಿ ತವಾಹಿತಾಃ ನಿನ್ದನ್ತಸ್ತವ ಸಾಮರ್ಥ್ಯಂ ತತೋ ದುಃಖತರಂ ನು ಕಿಮ್
roman: avācyavādāṃśca bahūnvadiṣyanti tavāhitāḥ nindantastava sāmarthyaṃ tato duḥkhataraṃ nu kim
trans: Your enemies will defame and humiliate you with unkind words, disparaging your might. Alas, what could be more painful than that?

kn: ಹತೋ ವಾ ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಸ್ಯಸಿ ಸ್ವರ್ಗಂ ಜಿತ್ವಾ ವಾ ಭೋಕ್ಷ್ಯಸೇ ಮಹೀಮ್ ತಸ್ಮಾದುತ್ತಿಷ್ಠ ಕೌನ್ತೇಯ ಯುದ್ಧಾಯ ಕೃತನಿಶ್ಚಯಃ
roman: hato vā prāpsyasi svargaṃ jitvā vā bhokṣyase mahīm tasmāduttiṣṭha kaunteya yuddhāya kṛtaniścayaḥ
trans: If you fight, you will either be slain on the battlefield and go to the celestial abodes, or you will gain victory and enjoy the kingdom on earth. Therefore arise with determination, O son of Kunti, and be prepared to fight.

kn: ಸುಖದುಃಖೇ ಸಮೇ ಕೃತ್ವಾ ಲಾಭಾಲಾಭೌ ಜಯಾಜಯೌ ತತೋ ಯುದ್ಧಾಯ ಯುಜ್ಯಸ್ವ ನೈವಂ ಪಾಪಮವಾಪ್ಸ್ಯಸಿ
roman: sukhaduḥkhe same kṛtvā lābhālābhau jayājayau tato yuddhāya yujyasva naivaṃ pāpamavāpsyasi
trans: Fight for the sake of duty, treating alike happiness and distress, loss and gain, victory and defeat. Fulfilling your responsibility in this way, you will never incur sin.

kn: ಏಷಾ ತೇಽಭಿಹಿತಾ ಸಾಙ್ಖ್ಯೇ ಬುದ್ಧಿರ್ಯೋಗೇ ತ್ವಿಮಾಂ ಶೃಣು ಬುದ್ಧ್ಯಾ ಯುಕ್ತೋ ಯಯಾ ಪಾರ್ಥ ಕರ್ಮಬನ್ಧಂ ಪ್ರಹಾಸ್ಯಸಿ
roman: eṣā te'bhihitā sāṅkhye buddhiryoge tvimāṃ śṛṇu buddhyā yukto yayā pārtha karmabandhaṃ prahāsyasi
trans: Hitherto, I have explained to you Sankhya Yog, or analytic knowledge regarding the nature of the soul. Now listen, O Parth, as I reveal Buddhi Yog, or the Yog of Intellect. When you work with such understanding, you will be freed from the bondage of karma.

kn: ನೇಹಾಭಿಕ್ರಮನಾಶೋಽಸ್ತಿ ಪ್ರತ್ಯವಾಯೋ ನ ವಿದ್ಯತೇ ಸ್ವಲ್ಪಮಪ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಧರ್ಮಸ್ಯ ತ್ರಾಯತೇ ಮಹತೋ ಭಯಾತ್
roman: nehābhikramanāśo'sti pratyavāyo na vidyate svalpamapyasya dharmasya trāyate mahato bhayāt
trans: Working in this state of consciousness, there is no loss or adverse result, and even a little effort saves one from great danger.

kn: ವ್ಯವಸಾಯಾತ್ಮಿಕಾ ಬುದ್ಧಿರೇಕೇಹ ಕುರುನನ್ದನ ಬಹುಶಾಖಾ ಹ್ಯನನ್ತಾಶ್ಚ ಬುದ್ಧಯೋಽವ್ಯವಸಾಯಿನಾಮ್
roman: vyavasāyātmikā buddhirekeha kurunandana bahuśākhā hyanantāśca buddhayo'vyavasāyinām
trans: O descendent of the Kurus, the intellect of those who are on this path is resolute, and their aim is one-pointed. But the intellect of those who are irresolute is many-branched.

kn: ಯಾಮಿಮಾಂ ಪುಷ್ಪಿತಾಂ ವಾಚಂ ಪ್ರವದನ್ತ್ಯವಿಪಶ್ಚಿತಃ ವೇದವಾದರತಾಃ ಪಾರ್ಥ ನಾನ್ಯದಸ್ತೀತಿ ವಾದಿನಃ
roman: yāmimāṃ puṣpitāṃ vācaṃ pravadantyavipaścitaḥ vedavādaratāḥ pārtha nānyadastīti vādinaḥ
trans: Those with limited understanding, get attracted to the flowery words of the Vedas, which advocate ostentatious rituals for elevation to the celestial abodes, and presume no higher principle is described in them.

kn: ಕಾಮಾತ್ಮಾನಃ ಸ್ವರ್ಗಪರಾ ಜನ್ಮಕರ್ಮಫಲಪ್ರದಾಮ್ ಕ್ರಿಯಾವಿಶೇಷಬಹುಲಾಂ ಭೋಗೈಶ್ವರ್ಯಗತಿಂ ಪ್ರತಿ
roman: kāmātmānaḥ svargaparā janmakarmaphalapradām kriyāviśeṣabahulāṃ bhogaiśvaryagatiṃ prati
trans: They glorify only those portions of the Vedas that please their senses, and perform pompous ritualistic ceremonies for attaining high birth, opulence, sensual enjoyment, and elevation to the heavenly planets.

kn: ಭೋಗೈಶ್ವರ್ಯಪ್ರಸಕ್ತಾನಾಂ ತಯಾಪಹೃತಚೇತಸಾಮ್ ವ್ಯವಸಾಯಾತ್ಮಿಕಾ ಬುದ್ಧಿಃ ಸಮಾಧೌ ನ ವಿಧೀಯತೇ
roman: bhogaiśvaryaprasaktānāṃ tayāpahṛtacetasām vyavasāyātmikā buddhiḥ samādhau na vidhīyate
trans: With their minds deeply attached to worldly pleasures and their intellects bewildered by such things, they are unable to possess the resolute determination for success on the path to God.

kn: ತ್ರೈಗುಣ್ಯವಿಷಯಾ ವೇದಾ ನಿಸ್ತ್ರೈಗುಣ್ಯೋ ಭವಾರ್ಜುನ ನಿರ್ದ್ವನ್ದ್ವೋ ನಿತ್ಯಸತ್ತ್ವಸ್ಥೋ ನಿರ್ಯೋಗಕ್ಷೇಮ ಆತ್ಮವಾನ್
roman: traiguṇyaviṣayā vedā nistraiguṇyo bhavārjuna nirdvandvo nityasattvastho niryogakṣema ātmavān
trans: The Vedas deal with the three modes of material nature, O Arjun. Rise above the three modes to a state of pure spiritual consciousness. Freeing yourself from dualities, eternally fixed in Truth, and without concern for material gain and safety, be situated in the self.

kn: ಯಾವಾನರ್ಥ ಉದಪಾನೇ ಸರ್ವತಃ ಸಮ್ಪ್ಲುತೋದಕೇ ತಾವಾನ್ಸರ್ವೇಷು ವೇದೇಷು ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮಣಸ್ಯ ವಿಜಾನತಃ
roman: yāvānartha udapāne sarvataḥ samplutodake tāvānsarveṣu vedeṣu brāhmaṇasya vijānataḥ
trans: Whatever purpose is served by a small well of water is naturally served in all respects by a large lake. Similarly, one who realizes the Absolute Truth also fulfills the purpose of all the Vedas.

kn: ಕರ್ಮಣ್ಯೇವಾಧಿಕಾರಸ್ತೇ ಮಾ ಫಲೇಷು ಕದಾಚನ ಮಾ ಕರ್ಮಫಲಹೇತುರ್ಭೂರ್ಮಾ ತೇ ಸಙ್ಗೋಽಸ್ತ್ವಕರ್ಮಣಿ
roman: karmaṇyevādhikāraste mā phaleṣu kadācana mā karmaphalaheturbhūrmā te saṅgo'stvakarmaṇi
trans: You have a right to perform your prescribed duties, but you are not entitled to the fruits of your actions. Never consider yourself to be the cause of the results of your activities, nor be attached to inaction.

kn: ಯೋಗಸ್ಥಃ ಕುರು ಕರ್ಮಾಣಿ ಸಙ್ಗಂ ತ್ಯಕ್ತ್ವಾ ಧನಞ್ಜಯ ಸಿದ್ಧ್ಯಸಿದ್ಧ್ಯೋಃ ಸಮೋ ಭೂತ್ವಾ ಸಮತ್ವಂ ಯೋಗ ಉಚ್ಯತೇ
roman: yogasthaḥ kuru karmāṇi saṅgaṃ tyaktvā dhanañjaya siddhyasiddhyoḥ samo bhūtvā samatvaṃ yoga ucyate
trans: Be steadfast in the performance of your duty, O Arjun, abandoning attachment to success and failure. Such equanimity is called Yog.

kn: ದೂರೇಣ ಹ್ಯವರಂ ಕರ್ಮ ಬುದ್ಧಿಯೋಗಾದ್ಧನಞ್ಜಯ ಬುದ್ಧೌ ಶರಣಮನ್ವಿಚ್ಛ ಕೃಪಣಾಃ ಫಲಹೇತವಃ
roman: dūreṇa hyavaraṃ karma buddhiyogāddhanañjaya buddhau śaraṇamanviccha kṛpaṇāḥ phalahetavaḥ
trans: Seek refuge in divine knowledge and insight, O Arjun, and discard reward-seeking actions that are certainly inferior to works performed with the intellect established in divine knowledge. Miserly are those who seek to enjoy the fruits of their works.

kn: ಬುದ್ಧಿಯುಕ್ತೋ ಜಹಾತೀಹ ಉಭೇ ಸುಕೃತದುಷ್ಕೃತೇ ತಸ್ಮಾದ್ಯೋಗಾಯ ಯುಜ್ಯಸ್ವ ಯೋಗಃ ಕರ್ಮಸು ಕೌಶಲಮ್
roman: buddhiyukto jahātīha ubhe sukṛtaduṣkṛte tasmādyogāya yujyasva yogaḥ karmasu kauśalam
trans: One who prudently practices the science of work without attachment can get rid of both good and bad reactions in this life itself. Therefore, strive for Yog, which is the art of working skillfully in proper consciousness.

kn: ಕರ್ಮಜಂ ಬುದ್ಧಿಯುಕ್ತಾ ಹಿ ಫಲಂ ತ್ಯಕ್ತ್ವಾ ಮನೀಷಿಣಃ ಜನ್ಮಬನ್ಧವಿನಿರ್ಮುಕ್ತಾಃ ಪದಂ ಗಚ್ಛನ್ತ್ಯನಾಮಯಮ್
roman: karmajaṃ buddhiyuktā hi phalaṃ tyaktvā manīṣiṇaḥ janmabandhavinirmuktāḥ padaṃ gacchantyanāmayam
trans: The wise endowed with equanimity of intellect, abandon attachment to the fruits of actions, which bind one to the cycle of life and death. By working in such consciousness, they attain the state beyond all suffering.

kn: ಯದಾ ತೇ ಮೋಹಕಲಿಲಂ ಬುದ್ಧಿರ್ವ್ಯತಿತರಿಷ್ಯತಿ ತದಾ ಗನ್ತಾಸಿ ನಿರ್ವೇದಂ ಶ್ರೋತವ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಶ್ರುತಸ್ಯ ಚ
roman: yadā te mohakalilaṃ buddhirvyatitariṣyati tadā gantāsi nirvedaṃ śrotavyasya śrutasya ca
trans: When your intellect crosses the quagmire of delusion, you will then acquire indifference to what has been heard and what is yet to be heard about enjoyments in this world and the next.

kn: ಶ್ರುತಿವಿಪ್ರತಿಪನ್ನಾ ತೇ ಯದಾ ಸ್ಥಾಸ್ಯತಿ ನಿಶ್ಚಲಾ ಸಮಾಧಾವಚಲಾ ಬುದ್ಧಿಸ್ತದಾ ಯೋಗಮವಾಪ್ಸ್ಯಸಿ
roman: śrutivipratipannā te yadā sthāsyati niścalā samādhāvacalā buddhistadā yogamavāpsyasi
trans: When your intellect ceases to be allured by the fruitive sections of the Vedas and remains steadfast in divine consciousness, you will then attain the state of perfect Yog.

kn: ಸ್ಥಿತಪ್ರಜ್ಞಸ್ಯ ಕಾ ಭಾಷಾ ಸಮಾಧಿಸ್ಥಸ್ಯ ಕೇಶವ ಸ್ಥಿತಧೀಃ ಕಿಂ ಪ್ರಭಾಷೇತ ಕಿಮಾಸೀತ ವ್ರಜೇತ ಕಿಮ್
roman: sthitaprajñasya kā bhāṣā samādhisthasya keśava sthitadhīḥ kiṃ prabhāṣeta kimāsīta vrajeta kim
trans: Arjun said: O Keshav, what is the disposition of one who is situated in divine consciousness? How does an enlightened person talk? How does he sit? How does he walk?

kn: ಪ್ರಜಹಾತಿ ಯದಾ ಕಾಮಾನ್ಸರ್ವಾನ್ಪಾರ್ಥ ಮನೋಗತಾನ್ ಆತ್ಮನ್ಯೇವಾತ್ಮನಾ ತುಷ್ಟಃ ಸ್ಥಿತಪ್ರಜ್ಞಸ್ತದೋಚ್ಯತೇ
roman: prajahāti yadā kāmānsarvānpārtha manogatān ātmanyevātmanā tuṣṭaḥ sthitaprajñastadocyate
trans: The Supreme Lord said: O Parth, when one discards all selfish desires and cravings of the senses that torment the mind, and becomes satisfied in the realization of the self, such a person is said to be transcendentally situated.

kn: ದುಃಖೇಷ್ವನುದ್ವಿಗ್ನಮನಾಃ ಸುಖೇಷು ವಿಗತಸ್ಪೃಹಃ ವೀತರಾಗಭಯಕ್ರೋಧಃ ಸ್ಥಿತಧೀರ್ಮುನಿರುಚ್ಯತೇ
roman: duḥkheṣvanudvignamanāḥ sukheṣu vigataspṛhaḥ vītarāgabhayakrodhaḥ sthitadhīrmunirucyate
trans: One whose mind remains undisturbed amidst misery, who does not crave for pleasure, and who is free from attachment, fear, and anger, is called a sage of steady wisdom.

kn: ಯಃ ಸರ್ವತ್ರಾನಭಿಸ್ನೇಹಸ್ತತ್ತತ್ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯ ಶುಭಾಶುಭಮ್ ನಾಭಿನನ್ದತಿ ನ ದ್ವೇಷ್ಟಿ ತಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾ ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಿತಾ
roman: yaḥ sarvatrānabhisnehastattatprāpya śubhāśubham nābhinandati na dveṣṭi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
trans: One who remains unattached under all conditions, and is neither delighted by good fortune nor dejected by tribulation, he is a sage with perfect knowledge.

kn: ಯದಾ ಸಂಹರತೇ ಚಾಯಂ ಕೂರ್ಮೋಽಙ್ಗಾನೀವ ಸರ್ವಶಃ ಇನ್ದ್ರಿಯಾಣೀನ್ದ್ರಿಯಾರ್ಥೇಭ್ಯಸ್ತಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾ ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಿತಾ
roman: yadā saṃharate cāyaṃ kūrmo'ṅgānīva sarvaśaḥ indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
trans: One who is able to withdraw the senses from their objects, just as a tortoise withdraws its limbs into its shell, is established in divine wisdom.

kn: ವಿಷಯಾ ವಿನಿವರ್ತನ್ತೇ ನಿರಾಹಾರಸ್ಯ ದೇಹಿನಃ ರಸವರ್ಜಂ ರಸೋಽಪ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಪರಂ ದೃಷ್ಟ್ವಾ ನಿವರ್ತತೇ
roman: viṣayā vinivartante nirāhārasya dehinaḥ rasavarjaṃ raso'pyasya paraṃ dṛṣṭvā nivartate
trans: Aspirants may restrain the senses from their objects of enjoyment, but the taste for the sense objects remains. However, even this taste ceases for those who realize the Supreme.

kn: ಯತತೋ ಹ್ಯಪಿ ಕೌನ್ತೇಯ ಪುರುಷಸ್ಯ ವಿಪಶ್ಚಿತಃ ಇನ್ದ್ರಿಯಾಣಿ ಪ್ರಮಾಥೀನಿ ಹರನ್ತಿ ಪ್ರಸಭಂ ಮನಃ
roman: yatato hyapi kaunteya puruṣasya vipaścitaḥ indriyāṇi pramāthīni haranti prasabhaṃ manaḥ
trans: The senses are so strong and turbulent, O son of Kunti, that they can forcibly carry away the mind even of a person endowed with discrimination who practices self-control.

kn: ತಾನಿ ಸರ್ವಾಣಿ ಸಂಯಮ್ಯ ಯುಕ್ತ ಆಸೀತ ಮತ್ಪರಃ ವಶೇ ಹಿ ಯಸ್ಯೇನ್ದ್ರಿಯಾಣಿ ತಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾ ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಿತಾ
roman: tāni sarvāṇi saṃyamya yukta āsīta matparaḥ vaśe hi yasyendriyāṇi tasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
trans: They are established in perfect knowledge, who subdue their senses and keep their minds ever absorbed in Me.

kn: ಧ್ಯಾಯತೋ ವಿಷಯಾನ್ಪುಂಸಃ ಸಙ್ಗಸ್ತೇಷೂಪಜಾಯತೇ ಸಙ್ಗಾತ್ಸಞ್ಜಾಯತೇ ಕಾಮಃ ಕಾಮಾತ್ಕ್ರೋಧೋಽಭಿಜಾಯತೇ
roman: dhyāyato viṣayānpuṃsaḥ saṅgasteṣūpajāyate saṅgātsañjāyate kāmaḥ kāmātkrodho'bhijāyate
trans: While contemplating on the objects of the senses, one develops attachment to them. Attachment leads to desire, and from desire arises anger.

kn: ಕ್ರೋಧಾದ್ಭವತಿ ಸಮ್ಮೋಹಃ ಸಮ್ಮೋಹಾತ್ಸ್ಮೃತಿವಿಭ್ರಮಃ ಸ್ಮೃತಿಭ್ರಂಶಾದ್ ಬುದ್ಧಿನಾಶೋ ಬುದ್ಧಿನಾಶಾತ್ಪ್ರಣಶ್ಯತಿ
roman: krodhādbhavati sammohaḥ sammohātsmṛtivibhramaḥ smṛtibhraṃśād buddhināśo buddhināśātpraṇaśyati
trans: Anger leads to clouding of judgment, which results in bewilderment of memory. When memory is bewildered, the intellect gets destroyed; and when the intellect is destroyed, one is ruined.

kn: ರಾಗದ್ವೇಷವಿಮುಕ್ತೈಸ್ತು ವಿಷಯಾನಿನ್ದ್ರಿಯೈಶ್ಚರನ್ ಆತ್ಮವಶ್ಯೈರ್ವಿಧೇಯಾತ್ಮಾ ಪ್ರಸಾದಮಧಿಗಚ್ಛತಿ
roman: rāgadveṣavimuktaistu viṣayānindriyaiścaran ātmavaśyairvidheyātmā prasādamadhigacchati
trans: But one who controls the mind, and is free from attachment and aversion, even while using the objects of the senses, attains the Grace of God.

kn: ಪ್ರಸಾದೇ ಸರ್ವದುಃಖಾನಾಂ ಹಾನಿರಸ್ಯೋಪಜಾಯತೇ ಪ್ರಸನ್ನಚೇತಸೋ ಹ್ಯಾಶು ಬುದ್ಧಿಃ ಪರ್ಯವತಿಷ್ಠತೇ
roman: prasāde sarvaduḥkhānāṃ hānirasyopajāyate prasannacetaso hyāśu buddhiḥ paryavatiṣṭhate
trans: By divine grace comes the peace in which all sorrows end, and the intellect of such a person of tranquil mind soon becomes firmly established in God.

kn: ನಾಸ್ತಿ ಬುದ್ಧಿರಯುಕ್ತಸ್ಯ ನ ಚಾಯುಕ್ತಸ್ಯ ಭಾವನಾ ನ ಚಾಭಾವಯತಃ ಶಾನ್ತಿರಶಾನ್ತಸ್ಯ ಕುತಃ ಸುಖಮ್
roman: nāsti buddhirayuktasya na cāyuktasya bhāvanā na cābhāvayataḥ śāntiraśāntasya kutaḥ sukham
trans: But an undisciplined person, who has not controlled the mind and senses, can neither have a resolute intellect nor steady contemplation on God. For one who never unites the mind with God there is no peace; and how can one who lacks peace be happy?

kn: ಇನ್ದ್ರಿಯಾಣಾಂ ಹಿ ಚರತಾಂ ಯನ್ಮನೋಽನುವಿಧೀಯತೇ ತದಸ್ಯ ಹರತಿ ಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾಂ ವಾಯುರ್ನಾವಮಿವಾಮ್ಭಸಿ
roman: indriyāṇāṃ hi caratāṃ yanmano'nuvidhīyate tadasya harati prajñāṃ vāyurnāvamivāmbhasi
trans: Just as a strong wind sweeps a boat off its chartered course on the water, even one of the senses on which the mind focuses can lead the intellect astray.

kn: ತಸ್ಮಾದ್ಯಸ್ಯ ಮಹಾಬಾಹೋ ನಿಗೃಹೀತಾನಿ ಸರ್ವಶಃ ಇನ್ದ್ರಿಯಾಣೀನ್ದ್ರಿಯಾರ್ಥೇಭ್ಯಸ್ತಸ್ಯ ಪ್ರಜ್ಞಾ ಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಿತಾ
roman: tasmādyasya mahābāho nigṛhītāni sarvaśaḥ indriyāṇīndriyārthebhyastasya prajñā pratiṣṭhitā
trans: Therefore, one who has restrained the senses from their objects, O mighty armed Arjun, is firmly established in transcendental knowledge.

kn: ಯಾ ನಿಶಾ ಸರ್ವಭೂತಾನಾಂ ತಸ್ಯಾಂ ಜಾಗರ್ತಿ ಸಂಯಮೀ ಯಸ್ಯಾಂ ಜಾಗ್ರತಿ ಭೂತಾನಿ ಸಾ ನಿಶಾ ಪಶ್ಯತೋ ಮುನೇಃ
roman: yā niśā sarvabhūtānāṃ tasyāṃ jāgarti saṃyamī yasyāṃ jāgrati bhūtāni sā niśā paśyato muneḥ
trans: What all beings consider as day is the night of ignorance for the wise, and what all creatures see as night is the day for the introspective sage.

kn: ಆಪೂರ್ಯಮಾಣಮಚಲಪ್ರತಿಷ್ಠಂ ಸಮುದ್ರಮಾಪಃ ಪ್ರವಿಶನ್ತಿ ಯದ್ವತ್ ತದ್ವತ್ಕಾಮಾ ಯಂ ಪ್ರವಿಶನ್ತಿ ಸರ್ವೇ ಸ ಶಾನ್ತಿಮಾಪ್ನೋತಿ ನ ಕಾಮಕಾಮೀ
roman: āpūryamāṇamacalapratiṣṭhaṃ samudramāpaḥ praviśanti yadvat tadvatkāmā yaṃ praviśanti sarve sa śāntimāpnoti na kāmakāmī
trans: Just as the ocean remains undisturbed by the incessant flow of waters from rivers merging into it, likewise the sage who is unmoved despite the flow of desirable objects all around him attains peace, and not the person who strives to satisfy desires.

kn: ವಿಹಾಯ ಕಾಮಾನ್ಯಃ ಸರ್ವಾನ್ಪುಮಾಂಶ್ಚರತಿ ನಿಃಸ್ಪೃಹಃ ನಿರ್ಮಮೋ ನಿರಹಙ್ಕಾರಃ ಸ ಶಾನ್ತಿಮಧಿಗಚ್ಛತಿ
roman: vihāya kāmānyaḥ sarvānpumāṃścarati niḥspṛhaḥ nirmamo nirahaṅkāraḥ sa śāntimadhigacchati
trans: That person, who gives up all material desires and lives free from a sense of greed, proprietorship, and egoism, attains perfect peace.

kn: ಏಷಾ ಬ್ರಾಹ್ಮೀ ಸ್ಥಿತಿಃ ಪಾರ್ಥ ನೈನಾಂ ಪ್ರಾಪ್ಯ ವಿಮುಹ್ಯತಿ ಸ್ಥಿತ್ವಾಸ್ಯಾಮನ್ತಕಾಲೇಽಪಿ ಬ್ರಹ್ಮನಿರ್ವಾಣಮೃಚ್ಛತಿ
roman: eṣā brāhmī sthitiḥ pārtha naināṃ prāpya vimuhyati sthitvāsyāmantakāle'pi brahmanirvāṇamṛcchati
trans: O Parth, such is the state of an enlightened soul that having attained it, one is never again deluded. Being established in this consciousness even at the hour of death, one is liberated from the cycle of life and death and reaches the Supreme Abode of God.
